Skim it once, keep it handy, and refer back whenever you are unsure.\n\n> **Note**: If you're using AI coding assistants, also see [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for AI-optimized quick reference.\n\n## Table of Contents\n\n- [Quick Start](#quick-start)\n- [Coding Standards](#coding-standards)\n- [Testing](#testing)\n- [Commit Guidelines](#commit-guidelines)\n- [Before Submitting](#before-submitting)\n- [Design Patterns Used in Fromager](#design-patterns-used-in-fromager)\n- [Quick Reference](#quick-reference)\n- [Getting Help](#getting-help)\n- [Resources](#resources)\n\n---\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### Prerequisites\n\n- Python 3.12 or newer\n\n- `hatch` for environment and task management\n\n  ```bash\n  pip install hatch\n  # or\n  pipx install hatch  # recommended\n  ```\n\n### Initial Setup\n\n```bash\n# 1. Fork the repository on GitHub\n# 2. Clone your fork\ngit clone https://github.com/<your-username>/fromager.git\ncd fromager\n\n# 3. Add upstream remote\ngit remote add upstream https://github.com/python-wheel-build/fromager.git\n\n# 4. Create development environment\nhatch env create\n\n# 5. Install pre-commit hooks (optional but recommended)\nhatch run lint:install-hooks\n```\n\n### Contribution Workflow\n\n```bash\n# 1. Sync with upstream\ngit checkout main\ngit fetch upstream\ngit merge upstream/main\n\n# 2. Create a feature branch\ngit checkout -b feat/<short-description>\n\n# 3. Make changes and test as you go\nhatch run test:test tests/test_<module>.py       # Test your specific changes\n\n# 4. Before committing, run full quality checks\nhatch run lint:precommit\n\n# 5. Commit using Conventional Commits\ngit commit -m \"feat(scope): short summary\"\n\n# 6. Push to your fork\ngit push origin feat/<short-description>\n\n# 7. Create a pull request on GitHub\n```\n\n### Pre-commit Hook (Recommended)\n\nTo ensure quality checks run automatically before each commit, install the pre-commit hooks that run linting, mypy type checking, and commit message validation:\n\n```bash\n# Install pre-commit hooks (run once after cloning)\nhatch run lint:install-hooks\n\n# The hooks automatically run linters before each commit and validate\n# that commit messages follow Conventional Commits format.\n\n# If a hook fails, it will prevent the commit and show helpful messages.\n# You can fix formatting issues automatically with:\nhatch run lint:fix\n```\n\nThe pre-commit hooks prevent commits that would fail CI quality checks, and enforce that all commit messages follow the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format documented in the [Commit Guidelines](#commit-guidelines) section.\n\n---\n\n## Coding Standards\n\n### Type Annotations\n\n- Every function (including tests) must annotate all parameters and return values.\n- Use modern `X | None` syntax instead of `Optional[X]` (PEP 604).\n- Prefer precise collection types (`list[str]`, `dict[str, int]`, etc.).\n\n```python\ndef process(data: str | None, count: int = 0) -> dict[str, int]:\n    \"\"\"Process the input and return aggregate counts.\"\"\"\n    return {}\n```\n\n### Code Quality and Formatting\n\n- Ruff enforces both formatting and linting.\n- Run `hatch run lint:fix` to automatically format code.\n- See [Quick Reference](#quick-reference) for additional commands.\n\n### Import Organization\n\n- **PEP 8: imports should be at the top**: All import statements must be placed at the top of the file, after module docstrings and before other code.\n- **No local imports**: Do not place import statements inside functions, methods, or conditional blocks.\n\n### Documentation Expectations\n\n- Add a module docstring describing purpose and high-level behavior.\n- Public functions and classes require docstrings that cover arguments, return values, and noteworthy behavior.\n- Keep prose short and imperative; explain \"why\" decisions when the code itself cannot.\n\n```python\ndef retry_on_exception(\n    exceptions: tuple[type[Exception], ...],\n    max_attempts: int = 5,\n) -> typing.Callable:\n    \"\"\"Retry decorated call on the provided exception types.\n\n    Args:\n        exceptions: Exception types that trigger a retry.\n        max_attempts: Maximum number of attempts.\n\n    Returns:\n        Decorator function.\n    \"\"\"\n    ...\n```\n\n### Commenting Guidelines\n\n- Write self-explanatory code; reserve comments for non-obvious intent or domain context.\n- Capture reasoning, invariants, or unexpected trade-offs—never repeat the code literally.\n\n```python\n# Bad - comment just repeats the code\nx = x + 1  # increment x\n\n# Good - clear variable name makes the comment unnecessary\ntotal_attempts += 1\n\n# Good - comment explains the reasoning behind the approach\n# Exponential backoff avoids thundering herd when many jobs retry at once.\nwait_time = min(2**attempt + random.uniform(0, 1), max_backoff)\n```\n\n### Logging\n\n- Use a module-level logger and the appropriate log level for the situation.\n- When processing per-requirement work, wrap nested calls in `req_ctxvar_context()` so log records automatically include the package (and optional version). This keeps CLI logs searchable even when work runs in parallel.\n\n```python\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\ndef sync_artifacts() -> None:\n    logger.info(\"Starting artifact sync\")\n    logger.debug(\"Artifacts queued: %s\", pending_jobs)\n\n# When processing a specific package, wrap calls to include package info in logs\n# req: Requirement object for the package being processed\n# version: Version string being built (optional)\nwith req_ctxvar_context(req, version):\n    logger.info(\"Resolving build dependencies\")  # Logs will include package name\n```\n\n### Error Handling\n\n- Raise specific exceptions with actionable messages.\n- Chain exceptions (`raise ... from e`) so stack traces stay informative.\n\n```python\ntry:\n    result = process_data(file_path)\nexcept FileNotFoundError as err:\n    raise ValueError(f\"Cannot load config at {file_path}\") from err\n```\n\n---\n\n## Testing\n\n### Structure\n\n- Place tests under `tests/`.\n- Name files `test_<module>.py` and functions `test_<behavior>()`.\n- Keep tests small: arrange, act, assert.\n\n```python\ndef test_load_config(tmp_path: pathlib.Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Verify config loads with expected values.\"\"\"\n    # Arrange\n    config_file = tmp_path / \"config.txt\"\n    config_file.write_text(\"setting=value\\n\")\n    # Act\n    result = load_config(config_file)\n    # Assert\n    assert result[\"setting\"] == \"value\"\n```\n\n### Useful Commands\n\n```bash\nhatch run test:test                              # Full suite\nhatch run test:test tests/test_context.py        # Specific file\nhatch run test:test --log-level DEBUG            # Verbose output\nhatch run test:coverage-report                   # Coverage summary\n```\n\n---\n\n## Commit Guidelines\n\nFromager follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/).\n\n```text\n<type>(<scope>): <short summary>\n\n<body explaining what + why>\n\n<footer for metadata>\n```\n\n### Common Types\n\n- `feat`: new functionality\n- `fix`: bug fix\n- `docs`: documentation only\n- `test`: tests only\n- `refactor`: behavioral no-op refactor\n- `perf`: performance improvement\n- `chore`: tooling or dependency change\n\n### Writing Tips\n\n- Subject ≤ 72 characters, imperative voice, no trailing period.\n- Describe motivation in the body if the diff is not self-explanatory.\n- Reference issues when relevant (`Closes: #123`).\n\n### Examples\n\n```text\nfeat(http_retry): add exponential backoff with jitter\n\nSupport transient failures more gracefully by adding jittered backoff.\n\nCloses: #456\n```\n\n```text\nfix(constraints): handle missing constraint file gracefully\n\nValidate file existence and emit a helpful message instead of crashing.\n```\n\n### AI-Generated Code Attribution\n\nWhen AI tools create or significantly modify code, add attribution:\n\n```text\nfeat(resolver): add exponential backoff for HTTP retries\n\nImproves resilience when PyPI is under load by adding jittered backoff.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude <claude@anthropic.com>\nCloses: #456\n```\n\nAvoid vague messages like `fix bug`, `update files`, or `WIP`.\n\n---\n\n## Before Submitting\n\n### Quality Checklist\n\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:fix`\n- [ ] `hatch run test:test`\n- [ ] `hatch run mypy:check`\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:check`\n\n### Code Review Checklist\n\n- [ ] Every function is fully typed.\n- [ ] Public APIs include docstrings.\n- [ ] Tests cover the change (positive + edge cases).\n- [ ] No trailing whitespace; files end with a newline.\n- [ ] Conventional Commit format followed.\n- [ ] Code aligns with existing patterns.\n\n---\n\n## Design Patterns Used in Fromager\n\n### Context Managers\n\n```python\n@contextlib.contextmanager\ndef resource_context() -> typing.Generator[None, None, None]:\n    \"\"\"Manage resource lifecycle.\"\"\"\n    setup_resource()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        cleanup_resource()\n```\n\n### Thread-Safe Decorators\n\n```python\ndef with_thread_lock() -> typing.Callable:\n    \"\"\"Create thread-safe wrapper.\"\"\"\n    lock = threading.Lock()\n\n    def decorator(func: typing.Callable) -> typing.Callable:\n        @functools.wraps(func)\n        def wrapper(*args: typing.Any, **kwargs: typing.Any) -> typing.Any:\n            with lock:\n                return func(*args, **kwargs)\n        return wrapper\n    return decorator\n```\n\n### Pydantic Validation\n\n```python\ndef _validate_envkey(value: typing.Any) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Normalize environment variable keys.\"\"\"\n    if isinstance(value, bool):\n        return \"1\" if value else \"0\"\n    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):\n        return str(value)\n    if isinstance(value, str):\n        return value.strip()\n    raise TypeError(f\"unsupported type {type(value)}: {value!r}\")\n\nEnvKey = typing.Annotated[str, BeforeValidator(_validate_envkey)]\n```\n\n---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n### Commands\n\n| Task | Command |\n| -- | -- |\n| Run tests | `hatch run test:test` |\n| Check code quality | `hatch run Stays on until \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\".\n---\n\n# caveman\n\nRespond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.\n\nCaveman is a voice, not broken grammar. Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEvery response, whole session, until user says \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present. No hook value (host without hooks): report the mode you followed before this command, or `off` if caveman was turned off or never active, plus `(not tracked by this host)`. Example: `Caveman mode: caveman (not tracked by this host)`. Loading this skill to answer status is not activation. Never infer a mode from the configured default.\n\n## Why\n\n1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.\n2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.\n3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.\n\nBad: \"Migration drop column backup first.\"\nGood: \"Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column.\"\n\n### 5. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. Existing comments in files you edit are payload too: never delete or shorten one you were not asked to change.\n\n### 7. Tool runs: bounded status\n\nNo text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.\n\n### 8. User's language\n\nCompress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.\n\n### 9. Never perform caveman\n\nNo \"caveman mode on\", no \"me think\", no \"Caveman:\" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.\n\n## When to break the rules\n\nPlain prose, then resume:\n\n1. Security warning.\n2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.\n3. Step order a fragment could scramble.\n4. User confused or repeats the question.\n5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.\n6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.\n7. You ask the user a question or offer options. Full sentences, so the answer comes back right first time.\n\n## Pre-send check\n\n1. First sentence announces what you will do? Delete.\n2. Last sentence recaps or offers help? Delete.\n3. Every not/never/no/only present? Every code span, path, number, error verbatim?\n4. Any sentence with two readings? The requirement to match.\n        max_age_cutoff: If set, reject candidates published before this time.\n            Age filtering is skipped for packages that have an exact\n            ``==`` pin Range constraints (``>=``,\n            ``<``, etc.) still go through age filtering normally.\n        age_fallback: Strategy when age filtering removes all candidates.\n            ``ALL`` (default) keeps every candidate with a warning.\n            ``NEWEST`` keeps only the single newest candidate.\n            ``NONE`` returns an empty list, letting the caller handle it.\n\n    Returns list of (url, version) tuples sorted by version (highest first).\n\n    IMPORTANT: This bypasses resolvelib's full resolver to collect all matching\n    candidates. Settings flow from YAML\nfiles on disk through a merge pipeline into a single facade object\nused by the build pipeline.\n\n.. seealso::\n\n   :doc:`/reference/config-reference` documents every configuration\n   field.  :doc:`architecture-overview` maps the major subsystems.\n\nSettings Loading Flow\n---------------------\n\n.. code-block:: text\n\n   CLI flags\n   (--settings-file, --settings-dir, --patches-dir)\n         │\n         ▼\n   Settings.from_files()\n   ├── Load settings.yaml ──► SettingsFile (global config)\n   └── Glob settings/*.yaml ──► PackageSettings (one per package)\n         │\n         ▼\n   Settings object (held by WorkContext)\n         │\n         │  package_build_info(\"torch\")  (on demand, cached)\n\n==> docs/concepts/hooks-and-overrides.rst <==\nHooks and Overrides\n===================\n\nFromager has two plugin systems that serve different purposes:\n**per-package overrides** replace default behavior for a specific\npackage, while **global hooks** broadcast notifications after events\nfor every package.\n\n.. seealso::\n\n   :doc:`architecture-overview` maps the major subsystems.\n   :doc:`/reference/hooks` documents each override hook's arguments and\n   return values.  :doc:`/customization` covers global hooks with code\n   examples.\n\nComparison\n----------\n\n.. list-table::\n   :header-rows: 1\n   :widths: 20 40 40\n\n   * - Aspect\n     - Per-Package Overrides\n     - Global Hooks\n   * - **Scope**\n     - One named package\n     - Every package\n   * - **Cardinality**\n     - At most one override module per package\n58:def find_and_invoke(\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

"""Tests for the iterative bootstrap implementation.

Tests cover:
- Phase class hierarchy: class variables and base class behavior
- WorkItem dataclass defaults and state accumulation
- _track_why context manager behavior
- create_unresolved_work_items helper
- Resolve.run() version expansion
- Start.run() graph addition and seen-check
- PrepareSource.run() all branches (prebuilt, source, cached, bad path)
- PrepareBuild.run() dep installation and extraction
- Build.run() conditional install and result construction
- ProcessInstallDeps.run() hooks, dep extraction, error modes
- Complete.run() cleanup
- _handle_phase_error for all three error modes
- End-to-end iterative loop with LIFO ordering
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import concurrent.futures
import logging
import pathlib
import typing
from unittest.mock import Mock, call, patch

import pytest
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.utils import canonicalize_name
from packaging.version import Version
from resolvelib.resolvers import ResolverException

from fromager import bootstrapper, build_environment
from fromager.bootstrapper._build import Build
from fromager.bootstrapper._complete import Complete
from fromager.bootstrapper._phase import Phase
from fromager.bootstrapper._prepare_build import PrepareBuild
from fromager.bootstrapper._prepare_source import PrepareSource
from fromager.bootstrapper._process_install_deps import ProcessInstallDeps
from fromager.bootstrapper._resolve import Resolve
from fromager.bootstrapper._start import Start, _re_resolve_url
from fromager.bootstrapper._types import (
    BootstrapPhase,
    PreparedSourceData,
    SourceBuildResult,
)
from fromager.bootstrapper._work_item import WorkItem
from fromager.context import WorkContext
from fromager.requirements_file import RequirementType, SourceType


def _make_resolved_future(
    result: typing.Any,
) -> concurrent.futures.Future[typing.Any]:
    """Return an already-completed Future carrying *result*."""
    future: concurrent.futures.Future[typing.Any] = concurrent.futures.Future()
    future.set_result(result)
    return future


def _make_work_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    req_type: RequirementType = RequirementType.INSTALL,
    why_snapshot: list | None = None,
    parent: tuple | None = None,
    source_url: str | None = None,
    version: str | None = None,
    build_env: build_environment.BuildEnvironment | None = None,
    sdist_root_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    unpack_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_result: SourceBuildResult | None = None,
    build_system_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_backend_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_sdist_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    pbi_pre_built: bool = False,
    cached_wheel_filename: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_sdist_only: bool = False,
) -> WorkItem:
    return WorkItem(
        req=Requirement(req),
        req_type=req_type,
        why_snapshot=why_snapshot or [],
        parent=parent,
        source_url=source_url,
        resolved_version=Version(version) if version else None,
        build_env=build_env,
        sdist_root_dir=sdist_root_dir,
        unpack_dir=unpack_dir,
        build_result=build_result,
        build_system_deps=build_system_deps if build_system_deps is not None else set(),
        build_backend_deps=build_backend_deps
        if build_backend_deps is not None
        else set(),
        build_sdist_deps=build_sdist_deps if build_sdist_deps is not None else set(),
        pbi_pre_built=pbi_pre_built,
        cached_wheel_filename=cached_wheel_filename,
        build_sdist_only=build_sdist_only,
    )


def _make_resolve_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    req_type: RequirementType = RequirementType.INSTALL,
    why_snapshot: list | None = None,
    parent: tuple | None = None,
) -> Resolve:
    return Resolve(
        WorkItem(
            req=Requirement(req),
            req_type=req_type,
            why_snapshot=why_snapshot or [],
            parent=parent,
        )
    )


def _make_start_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    req_type: RequirementType = RequirementType.INSTALL,
    source_url: str = "https://pypi.org/testpkg-1.0.tar.gz",
    version: str = "1.0",
    why_snapshot: list | None = None,
    parent: tuple | None = None,
) -> Start:
    return Start(
        WorkItem(
            req=Requirement(req),
            req_type=req_type,
            why_snapshot=why_snapshot or [],
            parent=parent,
            source_url=source_url,
            resolved_version=Version(version),
        )
    )


_PHASE_TO_CLASS: dict[BootstrapPhase, type[Phase]] = {
    BootstrapPhase.RESOLVE: Resolve,
    BootstrapPhase.START: Start,
    BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_SOURCE: PrepareSource,
    BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_BUILD: PrepareBuild,
    BootstrapPhase.BUILD: Build,
    BootstrapPhase.PROCESS_INSTALL_DEPS: ProcessInstallDeps,
    BootstrapPhase.COMPLETE: Complete,
}


def _make_build_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    version: str = "1.0",
    phase: BootstrapPhase = BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_SOURCE,
    source_url: str = "https://pypi.org/testpkg-1.0.tar.gz",
    build_env: build_environment.BuildEnvironment | None = None,
    sdist_root_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    unpack_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_result: SourceBuildResult | None = None,
    build_system_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_backend_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_sdist_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    pbi_pre_built: bool = False,
    cached_wheel_filename: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_sdist_only: bool = False,
) -> Phase:
    wi = WorkItem(
        req=Requirement(req),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        why_snapshot=[],

class Cart:
    def __init__(self, tax_rate=0.0):
        self.items = []
        self.tax_rate = tax_rate

    def add(self, price, qty=1):
        self.items.append((price, qty))

    def total(self):
        return compute_total(self.items, self.tax_rate)

def compute_total(items, tax_rate=0.0):
    """Return the total price of items with tax applied.

    items: iterable of (unit_price, quantity)
    """
    subtotal = sum(price * qty for price, qty in items)
    return round(subtotal * (1 + tax_rate), 2)

from app.config import load_config


def test_sections():
    cfg = load_config()
    assert set(cfg) == {"server", "database", "features"}
    assert cfg["server"]["host"] == "0.0.0.0"


def test_values_and_types():
    cfg = load_config()
    assert cfg == {
        "server": {"host": "0.0.0.0", "port": 8080, "debug": False},
        "database": {
            "url": "postgresql://localhost/app",
            "pool_size": 5,
            "timeout": 2.5,
        },
        "features": {"beta": True, "max_upload_mb": 25},
    }
    for section, key in (
        ("server", "port"),
        ("database", "pool_size"),
        ("features", "max_upload_mb"),
    ):
        assert type(cfg[section][key]) is int
    assert type(cfg["database"]["timeout"]) is float
    assert cfg["server"]["debug"] is False
    assert cfg["features"]["beta"] is True


def test_custom_path(tmp_path):
    path = tmp_path / "custom.toml"
    path.write_text('[server]\nhost = "localhost"\nport = 9000\n', encoding="utf-8")
    assert load_config(path) == {"server": {"host": "localhost", "port": 9000}}

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from collections.abc import Iterable, Sequence


def distance(a: Sequence[float], b: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    return math.hypot(a[0] - b[0], a[1] - b[1])


def perimeter(points: Sequence[Sequence[float]]) -> float:
    if len(points) < 2:
        return 0.0
    return sum(distance(points[i], points[(i + 1) % len(points)]) for i in range(len(points)))


def centroid(points: Sequence[Sequence[float]]) -> tuple[float, float] | None:
    if not points:
        return None
    n = len(points)
    return (sum(p[0] for p in points) / n, sum(p[1] for p in points) / n)


class Polygon:
    def __init__(
        self: Polygon, points: Iterable[Sequence[float]], name: str | None = None
    ) -> None:
        self.points = list(points)
        self.name = name

    def area(self: Polygon) -> float:
        s = 0.0
        for i, (x1, y1) in enumerate(self.points):
            x2, y2 = self.points[(i + 1) % len(self.points)]
            s += x1 * y2 - x2 * y1
        return abs(s) / 2

    def scaled(self: Polygon, factor: float) -> Polygon:
        return Polygon([(x * factor, y * factor) for x, y in self.points], self.name)

    def describe(self: Polygon) -> dict[str, str | int | float | None]:
        return {"name": self.name, "sides": len(self.points), "area": self.area()}

import time
from collections import OrderedDict


class LRUCache:
    def __init__(self, capacity, ttl=None, clock=time.monotonic):
        if capacity <= 0:
            raise ValueError("capacity must be positive")
        self.capacity = capacity
        self.ttl = ttl
        self.clock = clock
        self._values = OrderedDict()
        self._deadlines = OrderedDict()
        self._stats = dict(hits=0, misses=0, evictions=0, expirations=0)

    def _expire(self):
        if self.ttl is None:
            return
        now = self.clock()
        # Fixed TTL preserves deadline order independently of access recency.
        # Each entry is removed once, making cleanup amortized O(1).
        while self._deadlines:
            key, deadline = next(iter(self._deadlines.items()))
            if deadline > now:
                break
            self._deadlines.popitem(last=False)
            del self._values[key]
            self._stats["expirations"] += 1

    def get(self, key, default=None):
        self._expire()
        if key not in self._values:
            self._stats["misses"] += 1
            return default
        self._values.move_to_end(key)
        self._stats["hits"] += 1
        return self._values[key]

    def put(self, key, value):
        self._expire()
        self._values[key] = value
        self._values.move_to_end(key)
        if self.ttl is not None:
            self._deadlines[key] = self.clock() + self.ttl
            self._deadlines.move_to_end(key)
        if len(self._values) > self.capacity:
            evicted, _ = self._values.popitem(last=False)
            self._deadlines.pop(evicted, None)
            self._stats["evictions"] += 1

    def delete(self, key):
        self._expire()
        if key not in self._values:
            return False
        del self._values[key]
        self._deadlines.pop(key, None)
        return True

    def stats(self):
        self._expire()
        return self._stats.copy()

    def __len__(self):
        self._expire()
        return len(self._values)

    def __contains__(self, key):
        self._expire()
        return key in self._values

+import unittest
+
+from cachelib import LRUCache
+
+
+class LRUCacheTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_invalid_capacity(self):
+        for capacity in (0, -1):
+            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+                LRUCache(capacity)
+
+    def test_get_and_update_change_recency(self):
+        cache = LRUCache(2)
+        cache.put("a", 1)
+        cache.put("b", 2)
+        self.assertEqual(cache.get("a"), 1)
+        cache.put("c", 3)
+        self.assertNotIn("b", cache)
+        cache.put("a", 4)
+        cache.put("d", 5)
+        self.assertNotIn("c", cache)
+        self.assertEqual(cache.get("a"), 4)
+        self.assertEqual(cache.stats()["evictions"], 2)
+
+    def test_contains_does_not_change_recency(self):
+        cache = LRUCache(2)
+        cache.put("a", None)
+        cache.put("b", 2)
+        self.assertIn("a", cache)
+        self.assertEqual(len(cache), 2)
+        cache.put("c", 3)
+        self.assertNotIn("a", cache)
+        self.assertEqual(cache.stats()["hits"], 0)
+
+    def test_delete_defaults_and_stats_snapshot(self):
+        cache = LRUCache(1)
+        cache.put("a", None)
+        self.assertIsNone(cache.get("a", "default"))
+        self.assertTrue(cache.delete("a"))
+        self.assertFalse(cache.delete("a"))
+        self.assertEqual(cache.get("a", "default"), "default")
+        self.assertIsNone(cache.get("missing"))
+        expected = dict(hits=1, misses=2, evictions=0, expirations=0)
+        self.assertEqual(cache.stats(), expected)
+        cache.stats()["hits"] = 100
+        self.assertEqual(cache.stats(), expected)
+
+    def test_ttl_boundary_and_access_does_not_refresh(self):
+        now = [0]
+        cache = LRUCache(2, ttl=10, clock=lambda: now[0])
+        cache.put("a", 1)
+        now[0] = 9
+        self.assertEqual(cache.get("a"), 1)
+        now[0] = 10
+        self.assertEqual(cache.get("a", "expired"), "expired")
+        self.assertEqual(cache.stats(), dict(hits=1, misses=1, evictions=0, expirations=1))
+
+    def test_update_refreshes_ttl_and_expiry_precedes_eviction(self):
+        now = [0]
+        cache = LRUCache(2, ttl=10, clock=lambda: now[0])
+        cache.put("a", 1)
+        now[0] = 1
+        cache.put("b", 2)
+        now[0] = 2
+        cache.put("a", 3)
+        now[0] = 11
+        cache.put("c", 4)
+        self.assertIn("a", cache)
+        self.assertNotIn("b", cache)
+        self.assertEqual(len(cache), 2)
+        self.assertEqual(cache.stats()["evictions"], 0)
+        now[0] = 12
+        self.assertFalse(cache.delete("a"))
+        self.assertEqual(cache.stats()["expirations"], 2)
+
+    def test_len_and_contains_remove_expired_entries(self):
+        for operation in (len, lambda cache: "a" in cache):
+            now = [0]
+            cache = LRUCache(1, ttl=1, clock=lambda: now[0])
+            cache.put("a", 1)
+            now[0] = 1
+            self.assertFalse(operation(cache))
+            self.assertEqual(cache.stats()["expirations"], 1)
+
+    def test_no_ttl_and_nonpositive_ttl(self):
+        def unused_clock():
+            raise AssertionError("A cache without TTL should not read the clock")
+
+        cache = LRUCache(1, clock=unused_clock)
+        cache.put("a", 1)
+        self.assertEqual(cache.get("a"), 1)
+        for ttl in (0, -1):
+            cache = LRUCache(1, ttl=ttl, clock=lambda: 0)
+            cache.put("a", 1)
+            self.assertNotIn("a", cache)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

import unittest

from cachelib import LRUCache


class LRUCacheTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_invalid_capacity(self):
        for capacity in (0, -1):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                LRUCache(capacity)

    def test_get_and_update_change_recency(self):
        cache = LRUCache(2)
        cache.put("a", 1)
        cache.put("b", 2)
        self.assertEqual(cache.get("a"), 1)
        cache.put("c", 3)
        self.assertNotIn("b", cache)
        cache.put("a", 4)
        cache.put("d", 5)
        self.assertNotIn("c", cache)
        self.assertEqual(cache.get("a"), 4)
        self.assertEqual(cache.stats()["evictions"], 2)

    def test_contains_does_not_change_recency(self):
        cache = LRUCache(2)
        cache.put("a", None)
        cache.put("b", 2)
        self.assertIn("a", cache)
        self.assertEqual(len(cache), 2)
        cache.put("c", 3)
        self.assertNotIn("a", cache)
        self.assertEqual(cache.stats()["hits"], 0)

    def test_delete_defaults_and_stats_snapshot(self):
        cache = LRUCache(1)
        cache.put("a", None)
        self.assertIsNone(cache.get("a", "default"))
        self.assertTrue(cache.delete("a"))
        self.assertFalse(cache.delete("a"))
        self.assertEqual(cache.get("a", "default"), "default")
        self.assertIsNone(cache.get("missing"))
        expected = dict(hits=1, misses=2, evictions=0, expirations=0)
        self.assertEqual(cache.stats(), expected)
        cache.stats()["hits"] = 100
        self.assertEqual(cache.stats(), expected)

    def test_ttl_boundary_and_access_does_not_refresh(self):
        now = [0]
        cache = LRUCache(2, ttl=10, clock=lambda: now[0])
        cache.put("a", 1)
        now[0] = 9
        self.assertEqual(cache.get("a"), 1)
        now[0] = 10
        self.assertEqual(cache.get("a", "expired"), "expired")
        self.assertEqual(cache.stats(), dict(hits=1, misses=1, evictions=0, expirations=1))

    def test_update_refreshes_ttl_and_expiry_precedes_eviction(self):
        now = [0]
        cache = LRUCache(2, ttl=10, clock=lambda: now[0])
        cache.put("a", 1)
        now[0] = 1
        cache.put("b", 2)
        now[0] = 2
        cache.put("a", 3)
        now[0] = 11
        cache.put("c", 4)
        self.assertIn("a", cache)
        self.assertNotIn("b", cache)
        self.assertEqual(len(cache), 2)
        self.assertEqual(cache.stats()["evictions"], 0)
        now[0] = 12
        self.assertFalse(cache.delete("a"))
        self.assertEqual(cache.stats()["expirations"], 2)

    def test_len_and_contains_remove_expired_entries(self):
        for operation in (len, lambda cache: "a" in cache):
            now = [0]
            cache = LRUCache(1, ttl=1, clock=lambda: now[0])
            cache.put("a", 1)
            now[0] = 1
            self.assertFalse(operation(cache))
            self.assertEqual(cache.stats()["expirations"], 1)

    def test_no_ttl_and_nonpositive_ttl(self):
        def unused_clock():
            raise AssertionError("A cache without TTL should not read the clock")

        cache = LRUCache(1, clock=unused_clock)
        cache.put("a", 1)
        self.assertEqual(cache.get("a"), 1)
        for ttl in (0, -1):
            cache = LRUCache(1, ttl=ttl, clock=lambda: 0)
            cache.put("a", 1)
            self.assertNotIn("a", cache)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

import argparse
import json
import sys


def count(path):
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        text = f.read()
    return {"lines": text.count("\n"), "words": len(text.split()), "chars": len(text)}


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="wc")
    ap.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("files", nargs="+")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    total = {"lines": 0, "words": 0, "chars": 0}
    rc = 0
    files = []
    for path in args.files:
        try:
            c = count(path)
        except OSError as e:
            print(f"wc: {path}: {e.strerror}", file=sys.stderr)
            rc = 1
            continue
        if args.json:
            files.append({"path": path, **c})
        else:
            print(f"{c['lines']:>8}{c['words']:>8}{c['chars']:>8} {path}")
        for k in total:
            total[k] += c[k]
    if args.json:
        print(json.dumps({"files": files, "total": total}))
    elif len(args.files) > 1:
        print(f"{total['lines']:>8}{total['words']:>8}{total['chars']:>8} total")
    return rc

index f3451ff..bb8eeb9 100644

@@ -1,3 +1,7 @@
+import json
+
+import pytest
+
 from wc.cli import main
 
 
@@ -5,3 +9,53 @@ def test_text(tmp_path, capsys):
     p = tmp_path / "a.txt"; p.write_text("hello world\nbye\n")
     assert main([str(p)]) == 0
     assert capsys.readouterr().out == f"       2       3      16 {p}\n"
+
+
+def test_json(tmp_path, capsys):
+    first = tmp_path / "a.txt"
+    second = tmp_path / "b.txt"
+    first.write_text("hello world\nbye\n")
+    second.write_text("café")
+    assert main(["--json", str(first), str(second)]) == 0
+    output = capsys.readouterr()
+    assert output.err == ""
+    assert json.loads(output.out) == {
+        "files": [
+            {"path": str(first), "lines": 2, "words": 3, "chars": 16},
+            {"path": str(second), "lines": 0, "words": 1, "chars": 4},
+        ],
+        "total": {"lines": 2, "words": 4, "chars": 20},
+    }
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("json_mode", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("has_file", [False, True])
+def test_missing_file(tmp_path, capsys, json_mode, has_file):
+    missing = tmp_path / "missing.txt"
+    existing = tmp_path / "a.txt"
+    existing.write_text("hello\n")
+    paths = [str(existing), str(missing)] if has_file else [str(missing)]
+    assert main((["--json"] if json_mode else []) + paths) == 1
+    output = capsys.readouterr()
+    assert output.err == f"wc: {missing}: No such file or directory\n"
+    if json_mode:
+        assert json.loads(output.out) == {
+            "files": [{"path": str(existing), "lines": 1, "words": 1, "chars": 6}] if has_file else [],
+            "total": {"lines": 1, "words": 1, "chars": 6} if has_file else {"lines": 0, "words": 0, "chars": 0},
+        }
+    else:
+        assert output.out == (
+            f"       1       1       6 {existing}\n       1       1       6 total\n"
+            if has_file else ""
+        )
+
+
+def test_text_total(tmp_path, capsys):
+    path = tmp_path / "a.txt"
+    path.write_text("hello\n")
+    assert main([str(path), str(path)]) == 0
+    assert capsys.readouterr().out == (
+        f"       1       1       6 {path}\n"
+        f"       1       1       6 {path}\n"
+        "       2       2      12 total\n"
+    )

import json

import pytest

from wc.cli import main


def test_text(tmp_path, capsys):
    p = tmp_path / "a.txt"; p.write_text("hello world\nbye\n")
    assert main([str(p)]) == 0
    assert capsys.readouterr().out == f"       2       3      16 {p}\n"


def test_json(tmp_path, capsys):
    first = tmp_path / "a.txt"
    second = tmp_path / "b.txt"
    first.write_text("hello world\nbye\n")
    second.write_text("café")
    assert main(["--json", str(first), str(second)]) == 0
    output = capsys.readouterr()
    assert output.err == ""
    assert json.loads(output.out) == {
        "files": [
            {"path": str(first), "lines": 2, "words": 3, "chars": 16},
            {"path": str(second), "lines": 0, "words": 1, "chars": 4},
        ],
        "total": {"lines": 2, "words": 4, "chars": 20},
    }


@pytest.mark.parametrize("json_mode", [False, True])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("has_file", [False, True])
def test_missing_file(tmp_path, capsys, json_mode, has_file):
    missing = tmp_path / "missing.txt"
    existing = tmp_path / "a.txt"
    existing.write_text("hello\n")
    paths = [str(existing), str(missing)] if has_file else [str(missing)]
    assert main((["--json"] if json_mode else []) + paths) == 1
    output = capsys.readouterr()
    assert output.err == f"wc: {missing}: No such file or directory\n"
    if json_mode:
        assert json.loads(output.out) == {
            "files": [{"path": str(existing), "lines": 1, "words": 1, "chars": 6}] if has_file else [],
            "total": {"lines": 1, "words": 1, "chars": 6} if has_file else {"lines": 0, "words": 0, "chars": 0},
        }
    else:
        assert output.out == (
            f"       1       1       6 {existing}\n       1       1       6 total\n"
            if has_file else ""
        )


def test_text_total(tmp_path, capsys):
    path = tmp_path / "a.txt"
    path.write_text("hello\n")
    assert main([str(path), str(path)]) == 0
    assert capsys.readouterr().out == (
        f"       1       1       6 {path}\n"
        f"       1       1       6 {path}\n"
        "       2       2      12 total\n"
    )

"""Parse access logs and summarize their request statistics."""

from collections import Counter
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from math import ceil, isfinite
from typing import Iterable


@dataclass
class Record:
    ts: datetime
    method: str
    path: str
    status: int
    latency_ms: float
    bytes: int


@dataclass
class Summary:
    total: int
    malformed: int
    by_status: dict[int, int]
    by_method: dict[str, int]
    p50_latency_ms: float
    p95_latency_ms: float
    bytes_total: int
    error_rate: float
    top_paths: list[tuple[str, int]]


def parse_line(line: str) -> Record | None:
    """Return a record for a valid line, or None for a malformed line."""
    fields = line.split()
    if len(fields) not in (5, 6):
        return None
    timestamp, method, path, status, latency = fields[:5]
    try:
        ts = datetime.fromisoformat(timestamp.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        if ts.tzinfo is None or ts.utcoffset() is None:
            return None
        ts = ts.astimezone(timezone.utc)
        status_value = int(status)
        latency_value = float(latency)
        bytes_value = int(fields[5]) if len(fields) == 6 else 0
    except (ValueError, OverflowError):
        return None
    if not isfinite(latency_value):
        return None
    return Record(ts, method, path, status_value, latency_value, bytes_value)


def summarize(lines: Iterable[str]) -> Summary:
    """Summarize valid records, counting every malformed input line."""
    statuses: Counter[int] = Counter()
    methods: Counter[str] = Counter()
    paths: Counter[str] = Counter()
    latencies: list[float] = []
    malformed = bytes_total = errors = 0
    for line in lines:
        record = parse_line(line)
        if record is None:
            malformed += 1
            continue
        statuses[record.status] += 1
        methods[record.method] += 1
        paths[record.path] += 1
        latencies.append(record.latency_ms)
        bytes_total += record.bytes
        errors += record.status >= 500
    latencies.sort()
    total = len(latencies)
    return Summary(
        total=total,
        malformed=malformed,
        by_status=dict(statuses),
        by_method=dict(methods),
        p50_latency_ms=latencies[ceil(total * 0.50) - 1] if total else 0.0,
        p95_latency_ms=latencies[ceil(total * 0.95) - 1] if total else 0.0,
        bytes_total=bytes_total,
        error_rate=errors / total if total else 0.0,
        top_paths=sorted(paths.items(), key=lambda item: (-item[1], item[0]))[:5],
    )

@@ -0,0 +1,64 @@
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+
+from logstats.parse import parse_line, summarize
+
+
+def test_optional_bytes_and_utc_conversion():
+    record = parse_line("2026-10-01T14:00:00+02:00 GET /health 200 0.4")
+    assert record is not None
+    assert record.ts == datetime(2026, 10, 1, 12, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
+    assert record.ts.tzinfo is timezone.utc
+    assert record.bytes == 0
+    assert record.latency_ms == 0.4
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("line", [
+    "", "garbage line here",
+    "invalid GET / 200 1",
+    "2026-10-01T12:00:00 GET / 200 1",
+    "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET / invalid 1",
+    "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET / 200 invalid",
+    "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET / 200 nan",
+    "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET / 200 1 invalid",
+    "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET / 200 1 2 extra",
+])
+def test_malformed(line):
+    assert parse_line(line) is None
+
+
+def test_sample():
+    with (Path(__file__).parents[1] / "sample.log").open() as lines:
+        result = summarize(lines)
+    assert result.total == 5
+    assert result.malformed == 1
+    assert result.by_status == {200: 2, 201: 1, 404: 1, 500: 1}
+    assert result.by_method == {"GET": 4, "POST": 1}
+    assert result.p50_latency_ms == 12.5
+    assert result.p95_latency_ms == 120.0
+    assert result.bytes_total == 963
+    assert result.error_rate == 0.2
+    assert result.top_paths == [("/api/users", 3), ("/api/users/7", 1), ("/health", 1)]
+
+
+def test_empty_and_all_malformed():
+    for lines, malformed in [([], 0), (["bad", ""], 2)]:
+        result = summarize(lines)
+        assert result.total == 0
+        assert result.malformed == malformed
+        assert result.by_status == result.by_method == {}
+        assert result.p50_latency_ms == result.p95_latency_ms == 0.0
+        assert result.bytes_total == result.error_rate == 0
+        assert result.top_paths == []
+
+
+def test_nearest_rank_and_top_five_ties():
+    result = summarize(
+        f"2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET /{path} 200 {latency} 1"
+        for latency, path in enumerate("fedcba", start=1)
+    )
+    assert result.p50_latency_ms == 3.0
+    assert result.p95_latency_ms == 6.0
+    assert result.top_paths == [(f"/{path}", 1) for path in "abcde"]

Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.\n\nBad: \"Migration drop column backup first.\"\nGood: \"Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column.\"\n\n### 5. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. Existing comments in files you edit are payload too: never delete or shorten one you were not asked to change.\n\n### 7. Tool runs: bounded status\n\nNo text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.\n\n### 8. User's language\n\nCompress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.\n\n### 9. Never perform caveman\n\nNo \"caveman mode on\", no \"me think\", no \"Caveman:\" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.\n\n## When to break the rules\n\nPlain prose, then resume:\n\n1. Security warning.\n2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.\n3. Step order a fragment could scramble.\n4. User confused or repeats the question.\n5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.\n6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.\n7. You ask the user a question or offer options. Full sentences, so the answer comes back right first time.\n\n## Pre-send check\n\n1. First sentence announces what you will do? Delete.\n2. Last sentence recaps or offers help? Delete.\n3. Every not/never/no/only present? Every code span, path, number, error verbatim?\n4. Any sentence with two readings? from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from logstats.parse import parse_line, summarize


def test_optional_bytes_and_utc_conversion():
    record = parse_line("2026-10-01T14:00:00+02:00 GET /health 200 0.4")
    assert record is not None
    assert record.ts == datetime(2026, 10, 1, 12, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    assert record.ts.tzinfo is timezone.utc
    assert record.bytes == 0
    assert record.latency_ms == 0.4


@pytest.mark.parametrize("line", [
    "", "garbage line here",
    "invalid GET / 200 1",
    "2026-10-01T12:00:00 GET / 200 1",
    "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET / invalid 1",
    "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET / 200 invalid",
    "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET / 200 nan",
    "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET / 200 1 invalid",
    "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET / 200 1 2 extra",
])
def test_malformed(line):
    assert parse_line(line) is None


def test_sample():
    with (Path(__file__).parents[1] / "sample.log").open() as lines:
        result = summarize(lines)
    assert result.total == 5
    assert result.malformed == 1
    assert result.by_status == {200: 2, 201: 1, 404: 1, 500: 1}
    assert result.by_method == {"GET": 4, "POST": 1}
    assert result.p50_latency_ms == 12.5
    assert result.p95_latency_ms == 120.0
    assert result.bytes_total == 963
    assert result.error_rate == 0.2
    assert result.top_paths == [("/api/users", 3), ("/api/users/7", 1), ("/health", 1)]


def test_empty_and_all_malformed():
    for lines, malformed in [([], 0), (["bad", ""], 2)]:
        result = summarize(lines)
        assert result.total == 0
        assert result.malformed == malformed
        assert result.by_status == result.by_method == {}
        assert result.p50_latency_ms == result.p95_latency_ms == 0.0
        assert result.bytes_total == result.error_rate == 0
        assert result.top_paths == []


def test_nearest_rank_and_top_five_ties():
    result = summarize(
        f"2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET /{path} 200 {latency} 1"
        for latency, path in enumerate("fedcba", start=1)
    )
    assert result.p50_latency_ms == 3.0
    assert result.p95_latency_ms == 6.0
    assert result.top_paths == [(f"/{path}", 1) for path in "abcde"]

+def test_default_tags_are_independent():
+    warehouse = Warehouse("a")
+    warehouse.restock("bolt", 5)
+    warehouse.restock("nut", 2)
+    warehouse.stock["bolt"].tags.append("metal")
+    assert warehouse.stock["nut"].tags == []
+    other = Warehouse("b")
+    other.restock("bolt", 1)
+    assert other.stock["bolt"].tags == []
+
+
+def test_explicit_containers_are_preserved():
+    stock = {}
+    history = []
+    tags = ["metal"]
+    warehouse = Warehouse("a", stock, history)
+    warehouse.restock("bolt", 5, tags)
+    assert warehouse.stock is stock
+    assert warehouse.history is history
+    assert stock["bolt"].tags is tags
+    assert history == [("restock", "bolt", 5)]
+
+
+def test_restock_and_ship():
+    warehouse = Warehouse("a")
+    warehouse.restock("nut", 2)
+    warehouse.restock("bolt", 5, ["metal"])
+    warehouse.restock("bolt", 3)
+    warehouse.ship("bolt", 4)
+    assert warehouse.report() == {"bolt": 4, "nut": 2}
+    assert list(warehouse.report()) == ["bolt", "nut"]
+    assert warehouse.stock["bolt"].tags == ["metal"]
+    assert warehouse.history[-1] == ("ship", "bolt", 4)

import pytest

from inv.warehouse import Warehouse


def test_independent_warehouses():
    a = Warehouse("a")
    a.restock("bolt", 5)
    b = Warehouse("b")
    assert b.report() == {}
    b.restock("nut", 2)
    assert a.report() == {"bolt": 5}
    assert len(b.history) == 1


def test_default_tags_are_independent():
    warehouse = Warehouse("a")
    warehouse.restock("bolt", 5)
    warehouse.restock("nut", 2)
    warehouse.stock["bolt"].tags.append("metal")
    assert warehouse.stock["nut"].tags == []
    other = Warehouse("b")
    other.restock("bolt", 1)
    assert other.stock["bolt"].tags == []


def test_explicit_containers_are_preserved():
    stock = {}
    history = []
    tags = ["metal"]
    warehouse = Warehouse("a", stock, history)
    warehouse.restock("bolt", 5, tags)
    assert warehouse.stock is stock
    assert warehouse.history is history
    assert stock["bolt"].tags is tags
    assert history == [("restock", "bolt", 5)]


def test_restock_and_ship():
    warehouse = Warehouse("a")
    warehouse.restock("nut", 2)
    warehouse.restock("bolt", 5, ["metal"])
    warehouse.restock("bolt", 3)
    warehouse.ship("bolt", 4)
    assert warehouse.report() == {"bolt": 4, "nut": 2}
    assert list(warehouse.report()) == ["bolt", "nut"]
    assert warehouse.stock["bolt"].tags == ["metal"]
    assert warehouse.history[-1] == ("ship", "bolt", 4)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="insufficient stock"):
        warehouse.ship("bolt", 5)
    assert warehouse.report() == {"bolt": 4, "nut": 2}
    assert len(warehouse.history) == 4

from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass
class Item:
    sku: str
    qty: int = 0
    tags: list = field(default_factory=list)


class Warehouse:
    def __init__(self, name, stock=None, history=None):
        self.name = name
        self.stock = {} if stock is None else stock
        self.history = [] if history is None else history

    def restock(self, sku, qty, tags=None):
        item = self.stock.get(sku)
        if item is None:
            item = Item(sku, 0, [] if tags is None else tags)
            self.stock[sku] = item
        item.qty += qty
        self.history.append(("restock", sku, qty))

    def ship(self, sku, qty):
        item = self.stock[sku]
        if item.qty < qty:
            raise ValueError("insufficient stock")
        item.qty -= qty
        self.history.append(("ship", sku, qty))

    def report(self):
        return {sku: item.qty for sku, item in sorted(self.stock.items())}

from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo


def next_run(now: datetime, hour: int, minute: int, tz: str) -> datetime:
    """Next hour:minute in tz strictly after now. `now` may be naive (treated as UTC) or aware."""
    if now.tzinfo is None:
        now = now.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    zone = ZoneInfo(tz)
    today = now.astimezone(zone).date()
    candidate = datetime(today.year, today.month, today.day, hour, minute, tzinfo=zone)
    if candidate <= now:
        # Advance the local calendar date, preserving the requested wall-clock time.
        tomorrow = today + timedelta(days=1)
        candidate = datetime(tomorrow.year, tomorrow.month, tomorrow.day, hour, minute, tzinfo=zone)
    return candidate

 from datetime import datetime, timezone
+from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo
+
+import pytest
 
 from sched import next_run
 
@@ -8,3 +11,31 @@ def test_result_is_after_now_late_evening_utc():
     nxt = next_run(now, 1, 0, "Europe/Berlin")
     assert nxt > now
     assert (nxt.year, nxt.month, nxt.day, nxt.hour) == (2026, 6, 3, 1)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "now, expected",
+    [
+        (datetime(2026, 3, 28, 4, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc), datetime(2026, 3, 29, 4, 30)),
+        (datetime(2026, 10, 24, 4, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc), datetime(2026, 10, 25, 4, 30)),
+    ],
+)
+def test_preserves_wall_clock_time_across_dst(now, expected):
+    zone = ZoneInfo("Europe/Berlin")
+    nxt = next_run(now, 4, 30, zone.key)
+    assert nxt == expected.replace(tzinfo=zone)
+    assert nxt > now
+    assert nxt.tzinfo == zone
+
+
+def test_equal_time_advances_to_next_day():
+    zone = ZoneInfo("Europe/Berlin")
+    now = datetime(2026, 6, 2, 1, 0, tzinfo=zone)
+    assert next_run(now, 1, 0, zone.key) == datetime(2026, 6, 3, 1, 0, tzinfo=zone)
+
+
+def test_naive_now_is_treated_as_utc():
+    now = datetime(2026, 6, 1, 23, 30)
+    assert next_run(now, 1, 0, "Europe/Berlin") == datetime(
+        2026, 6, 3, 1, 0, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("Europe/Berlin")
+    )

from datetime import datetime, timezone
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import pytest

from sched import next_run


def test_result_is_after_now_late_evening_utc():
    now = datetime(2026, 6, 1, 23, 30, tzinfo=timezone.utc)   # already 01:30 on June 2 in Berlin
    nxt = next_run(now, 1, 0, "Europe/Berlin")
    assert nxt > now
    assert (nxt.year, nxt.month, nxt.day, nxt.hour) == (2026, 6, 3, 1)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "now, expected",
    [
        (datetime(2026, 3, 28, 4, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc), datetime(2026, 3, 29, 4, 30)),
        (datetime(2026, 10, 24, 4, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc), datetime(2026, 10, 25, 4, 30)),
    ],
)
def test_preserves_wall_clock_time_across_dst(now, expected):
    zone = ZoneInfo("Europe/Berlin")
    nxt = next_run(now, 4, 30, zone.key)
    assert nxt == expected.replace(tzinfo=zone)
    assert nxt > now
    assert nxt.tzinfo == zone


def test_equal_time_advances_to_next_day():
    zone = ZoneInfo("Europe/Berlin")
    now = datetime(2026, 6, 2, 1, 0, tzinfo=zone)
    assert next_run(now, 1, 0, zone.key) == datetime(2026, 6, 3, 1, 0, tzinfo=zone)


def test_naive_now_is_treated_as_utc():
    now = datetime(2026, 6, 1, 23, 30)
    assert next_run(now, 1, 0, "Europe/Berlin") == datetime(
        2026, 6, 3, 1, 0, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("Europe/Berlin")
    )

import threading
import time


class Counter:
    """Named counters. Intended to be shared across request-handler threads."""

    def __init__(self):
        self._values = {}
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    def incr(self, name, by=1):
        with self._lock:
            current = self._values.get(name, 0)
            time.sleep(0)  # yield, simulates real work between read and write
            self._values[name] = current + by

    def get(self, name):
        with self._lock:
            return self._values.get(name, 0)

    def snapshot(self):
        with self._lock:
            return dict(self._values)

    def reset(self, name=None):
        with self._lock:
            if name is None:
                self._values.clear()
            else:
                self._values.pop(name, None)

import threading

from metrics import Counter


def test_no_lost_updates():
    c = Counter()

    def work():
        for _ in range(2000):
            c.incr("hits")

    ts = [threading.Thread(target=work) for _ in range(8)]
    [t.start() for t in ts]; [t.join() for t in ts]
    assert c.get("hits") == 16000


def test_snapshot_is_an_independent_plain_dict():
    c = Counter()
    c.incr("hits", 2)
    snapshot = c.snapshot()
    assert type(snapshot) is dict
    c.incr("hits")
    c.reset("hits")
    assert snapshot == {"hits": 2}
    snapshot["other"] = 10
    assert c.snapshot() == {}


def test_reset_one_or_all_counters():
    c = Counter()
    c.incr("hits")
    c.incr("misses", 2)
    c.reset("hits")
    assert c.get("hits") == 0
    assert c.snapshot() == {"misses": 2}
    c.reset()
    assert c.snapshot() == {}

from .registry import UnknownFormat, get


def _extension(fmt):
    return get(fmt).extension


def export_records(records, fmt):
    """records: list of dicts with identical keys. Returns bytes."""
    return get(fmt)().dump(records)


def export_to_file(records, fmt, path):
    exporter = get(fmt)()
    path = str(path)
    if not path.endswith(exporter.extension):
        path += exporter.extension
    with open(path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(exporter.dump(records))
    return path

import csv
import io

from ..registry import Exporter, register


@register
class CSVExporter(Exporter):
    name = "csv"
    extension = ".csv"

    def dump(self, records) -> bytes:
        buf = io.StringIO()
        if records:
            w = csv.DictWriter(buf, fieldnames=list(records[0].keys()), lineterminator="\n")
            w.writeheader()
            w.writerows(records)
        return buf.getvalue().encode()

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod


class UnknownFormat(ValueError):
    pass


class Exporter(ABC):
    name: str
    extension: str

    @abstractmethod
    def dump(self, records) -> bytes:
        """Serialize records into bytes."""


_exporters = {}


def register(exporter_cls):
    """Register an exporter class, returning it for decorator use."""
    _exporters[exporter_cls.name] = exporter_cls
    return exporter_cls


def get(name):
    """Return the exporter class registered under name."""
    try:
        return _exporters[name]
    except KeyError:
        raise UnknownFormat(
            f"Unknown format {name!r}. Known formats: {', '.join(names())}"
        ) from None


def names():
    return sorted(_exporters)

+from xml.sax.saxutils import escape
+
+from ..registry import Exporter, register
+
+
+@register
+class XMLExporter(Exporter):
+    name = "xml"
+    extension = ".xml"
+
+    def dump(self, records) -> bytes:
+        parts = ["<records>"]
+        for r in records:
+            parts.append("  <record>")
+            for k, v in r.items():
+                parts.append(f"    <{k}>{escape(str(v))}</{k}>")
+            parts.append("  </record>")
+        parts.append("</records>")
+        return ("\n".join(parts) + "\n").encode()

+from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
+
+
+class UnknownFormat(ValueError):
+    pass
+
+
+class Exporter(ABC):
+    name: str
+    extension: str
+
+    @abstractmethod
+    def dump(self, records) -> bytes:
+        """Serialize records into bytes."""
+
+
+_exporters = {}
+
+
+def register(exporter_cls):
+    """Register an exporter class, returning it for decorator use."""
+    _exporters[exporter_cls.name] = exporter_cls
+    return exporter_cls
+
+
+def get(name):
+    """Return the exporter class registered under name."""
+    try:
+        return _exporters[name]
+    except KeyError:
+        raise UnknownFormat(
+            f"Unknown format {name!r}. Known formats: {', '.join(names())}"
+        ) from None
+
+
+def names():
+    return sorted(_exporters)

import json
import pytest

from export import export_records, export_to_file, UnknownFormat
from export import Exporter, get, names, register, registry

R = [{"id": 1, "name": "a&b"}, {"id": 2, "name": "c"}]


def test_csv():
    assert export_records(R, "csv") == b"id,name\n1,a&b\n2,c\n"


def test_json():
    assert json.loads(export_records(R, "json")) == R


def test_xml():
    assert b"<name>a&amp;b</name>" in export_records(R, "xml")


def test_file_extension(tmp_path):
    p = export_to_file(R, "json", tmp_path / "out")
    assert p.endswith(".json")


def test_unknown():
    try:
        export_records(R, "yaml")
    except UnknownFormat:
        pass
    else:
        raise AssertionError


def test_builtin_registry():
    assert names() == ["csv", "json", "xml"]
    for name in names():
        assert issubclass(get(name), Exporter)
        assert get(name).extension == "." + name


@pytest.mark.parametrize("fmt, expected", [
    ("csv", b""),
    ("json", b"[]\n"),
    ("xml", b"<records>\n</records>\n"),
])
def test_empty_records(fmt, expected):
    assert export_records([], fmt) == expected


def test_custom_exporter(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(registry, "_exporters", registry._exporters.copy())

    @register
    class TextExporter(Exporter):
        name = "text"
        extension = ".txt"

        def dump(self, records) -> bytes:
            return str(len(records)).encode()

    assert get("text") is TextExporter
    assert "text" in names()
    assert export_records(R, "text") == b"2"
    path = tmp_path / "out.txt"
    assert export_to_file(R, "text", path) == str(path)
    assert path.read_bytes() == b"2"
    assert export_to_file(R, "text", tmp_path / "other").endswith(".txt")


def test_unknown_lists_formats_and_does_not_create_file(tmp_path):
    path = tmp_path / "out"
    for operation in (
        lambda: export_records(R, "yaml"),
        lambda: export_to_file(R, "yaml", path),
    ):
        with pytest.raises(UnknownFormat) as error:
            operation()
        assert "yaml" in str(error.value)
        for name in names():
            assert name in str(error.value)
    assert not path.exists()

from xml.sax.saxutils import escape

from ..registry import Exporter, register


@register
class XMLExporter(Exporter):
    name = "xml"
    extension = ".xml"

    def dump(self, records) -> bytes:
        parts = ["<records>"]
        for r in records:
            parts.append("  <record>")
            for k, v in r.items():
                parts.append(f"    <{k}>{escape(str(v))}</{k}>")
            parts.append("  </record>")
        parts.append("</records>")
        return ("\n".join(parts) + "\n").encode()

import asyncio


class FetchError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, url, cause):
        super().__init__(f"{url}: {cause}")
        self.url = url
        self.cause = cause


class TransientError(Exception):
    pass


async def default_transport(url):
    await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
    if url.endswith("/404"):
        raise KeyError("not found")
    return f"payload for {url}".encode()


class Client:
    def __init__(self, transport=None, retries=3, backoff=0.01, max_concurrency=5):
        if max_concurrency < 1:
            raise ValueError("max_concurrency must be positive")
        self.transport = transport or default_transport
        self._semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrency)
        self.retries = retries
        self.backoff = backoff
        self.closed = False
        self.calls = 0

    async def get(self, url):
        if self.closed:
            raise RuntimeError("client closed")
        delay = self.backoff
        for attempt in range(1, self.retries + 1):
            self.calls += 1
            try:
                return await self.transport(url)
            except TransientError:
                if attempt == self.retries:
                    raise
                await asyncio.sleep(delay)
                delay *= 2

    async def get_many(self, urls):
        async def fetch(url):
            async with self._semaphore:
                try:
                    return await self.get(url)
                except Exception as e:
                    return FetchError(url, e)

        return await asyncio.gather(*(fetch(url) for url in urls))

    async def close(self):
        self.closed = True

    async def __aenter__(self):
        return self

    async def __aexit__(self, *exc):
        await self.close()

again\")\n        return b\"ok\"\n\n    c = Client(transport=flaky, retries=3)\n    assert c.get(\"u\") == b\"ok\" and c.calls == 3\n\n\ndef test_summarize():\n    c = Client()\n    assert aggregate.summarize(c, [\"http://x/1\", \"http://x/404\"]) == {\n        \"ok\": 1, \"failed\": [\"http://x/404\"], \"bytes\": len(b\"payload for http://x/1\")}\n---\nname: caveman\ndescription: >\n  Terse caveman voice: answer first, fluff gone, every technical fact kept.\n  Use for /caveman, \"caveman mode\", \"talk like caveman\", \"be brief\", \"less\n  tokens\". Stays on until \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\".\n---\n\n# caveman\n\nRespond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.\n\nCaveman is a voice, not broken grammar. Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEvery response, whole session, until user says \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present. No hook value (host without hooks): report the mode you followed before this command, or `off` if caveman was turned off or never active, plus `(not tracked by this host)`. Example: `Caveman mode: caveman (not tracked by this host)`. Loading this skill to answer status is not activation. Never infer a mode from the configured default.\n\n## Why\n\n1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.\n2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.\n3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.\n\nBad: \"Migration drop column backup first.\"\nGood: \"Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column.\"\n\n### 5. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. Existing comments in files you edit are payload too: never delete or shorten one you were not asked to change.\n\n### 7. Tool runs: bounded status\n\nNo text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.\n\n### 8. User's language\n\nCompress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.\n\n### 9. Never perform caveman\n\nNo \"caveman mode on\", no \"me think\", no \"Caveman:\" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.\n\n## When to break the rules\n\nPlain prose, then resume:\n\n1. Security warning.\n2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.\n3. Step order a fragment could scramble.\n4. User confused or repeats the question.\n5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.\n6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.\n7. You ask the user a question or offer options. Full sentences, so the answer comes back right first time.\n\n## Pre-send check\n\n1. First sentence announces what you will do? Delete.\n2. Last sentence recaps or offers help? Delete.\n3. Every not/never/no/only present? Every code span, path, number, error verbatim?\n4. Any sentence with two readings? Make it a full sentence.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

import asyncio

from .client import Client


def fetch_all(urls, transport=None):
    async def fetch():
        async with Client(transport) as client:
            return await client.get_many(urls)

    return asyncio.run(fetch())

import asyncio

import pytest

from fetcher import Client, FetchError, TransientError, aggregate
from fetcher.sync import fetch_all


def test_get_and_many():
    async def run():
        async with Client() as c:
            assert await c.get("http://x/1") == b"payload for http://x/1"
            res = await c.get_many(["http://x/1", "http://x/404"])
            assert res[0].startswith(b"payload") and isinstance(res[1], FetchError)
            assert res[1].url == "http://x/404"
            assert isinstance(res[1].cause, KeyError)
        assert c.closed
        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="client closed"):
            await c.get("u")
        assert isinstance((await c.get_many(["u"]))[0], FetchError)

    asyncio.run(run())


def test_retry_then_succeed():
    async def run():
        attempts = {"n": 0}

        async def flaky(url):
            attempts["n"] += 1
            if attempts["n"] < 3:
                raise TransientError("try again")
            return b"ok"

        async with Client(transport=flaky, retries=3) as c:
            assert await c.get("u") == b"ok" and c.calls == 3

    asyncio.run(run())


def test_summarize():
    async def run():
        async with Client() as c:
            assert await aggregate.summarize(c, ["http://x/1", "http://x/404"]) == {
                "ok": 1, "failed": ["http://x/404"],
                "bytes": len(b"payload for http://x/1")}
            assert await aggregate.summarize(c, []) == {
                "ok": 0, "failed": [], "bytes": 0}

    asyncio.run(run())


def test_concurrency_and_order():
    async def run():
        active = 0
        peak = 0

        async def transport(url):
            nonlocal active, peak
            active += 1
            peak = max(peak, active)
            await asyncio.sleep(0.001 * (6 - int(url)))
            active -= 1
            return url.encode()

        async with Client(transport, max_concurrency=2) as c:
            assert await c.get_many(str(i) for i in range(6)) == [
                str(i).encode() for i in range(6)]
            assert peak == 2
            assert await c.get_many([]) == []

    asyncio.run(run())


def test_retry_policy(monkeypatch):
    delays = []

    async def sleep(delay):
        delays.append(delay)

    monkeypatch.setattr(asyncio, "sleep", sleep)

    async def run():
        async def transient(url):
            raise TransientError("retry")

        async with Client(transient, retries=3, backoff=0.25) as c:
            result = (await c.get_many(["u"]))[0]
            assert isinstance(result, FetchError)
            assert isinstance(result.cause, TransientError)
            assert c.calls == 3
            assert delays == [0.25, 0.5]

        async def permanent(url):
            raise ValueError("permanent")

        async with Client(permanent) as c:
            with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="permanent"):
                await c.get("u")
            assert c.calls == 1
            assert delays == [0.25, 0.5]

    asyncio.run(run())


def test_cancellation_and_context_cleanup():
    async def run():
        async def transport(url):
            raise asyncio.CancelledError()

        c = Client(transport)
        with pytest.raises(asyncio.CancelledError):
            async with c:
                await c.get_many(["u"])
        assert c.closed
        await c.close()

    asyncio.run(run())


def test_sync_wrapper():
    assert fetch_all(["http://x/1"]) == [b"payload for http://x/1"]

    async def transport(url):
        if url == "bad":
            raise ValueError("bad")
        return url.encode()

    results = fetch_all(["good", "bad"], transport)
    assert results[0] == b"good"
    assert isinstance(results[1], FetchError)
    assert isinstance(results[1].cause, ValueError)


def test_invalid_concurrency():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="max_concurrency must be positive"):
        Client(max_concurrency=0)
