{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_4","type":"command_execution","command":"/usr/bin/bash -lc \"cat /home/alustosa/.codex/plugins/cache/caveman/caveman/3.2.0/skills/caveman/SKILL.md; rg --files -g '\"'!**/__pycache__/**'\"' -g '\"'!*.pyc'\"'; ls -la\"","aggregated_output":"---\nname: caveman\ndescription: >\n  Terse caveman voice: answer first, fluff gone, every technical fact kept.\n  Use for /caveman, \"caveman mode\", \"talk like caveman\", \"be brief\", \"less\n  tokens\". Stays on until \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\".\n---\n\n# caveman\n\nRespond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.\n\nCaveman is a voice, not broken grammar. Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEvery response, whole session, until user says \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present. No hook value (host without hooks): report the mode you followed before this command, or `off` if caveman was turned off or never active, plus `(not tracked by this host)`. Example: `Caveman mode: caveman (not tracked by this host)`. Loading this skill to answer status is not activation. Never infer a mode from the configured default.\n\n## Why\n\n1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.\n2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.\n3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.\n\nBad: \"Migration drop column backup first.\"\nGood: \"Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column.\"\n\n### 5. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. Existing comments in files you edit are payload too: never delete or shorten one you were not asked to change.\n\n### 7. Tool runs: bounded status\n\nNo text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.\n\n### 8. User's language\n\nCompress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.\n\n### 9. Never perform caveman\n\nNo \"caveman mode on\", no \"me think\", no \"Caveman:\" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.\n\n## When to break the rules\n\nPlain prose, then resume:\n\n1. Security warning.\n2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.\n3. Step order a fragment could scramble.\n4. User confused or repeats the question.\n5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.\n6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.\n7. You ask the user a question or offer options. Full sentences, so the answer comes back right first time.\n\n## Pre-send check\n\n1. First sentence announces what you will do? Delete.\n2. Last sentence recaps or offers help? Delete.\n3. Every not/never/no/only present? Every code span, path, number, error verbatim?\n4. Any sentence with two readings? from decimal import Decimal

import pytest

from billing import build_invoice, percent_off, invoice_total, line_totals, TaxRule
from billing.render import render


def test_simple_total():
    inv = build_invoice("A1", [("x", "10.00", 2), ("y", "0.50", 1)])
    assert invoice_total(inv) == Decimal("20.50")
    assert sum(line_totals(inv)) == Decimal("20.50")


def test_with_tax():
    inv = build_invoice("A2", [("x", "100.00", 1)], TaxRule("DE", Decimal("0.19")))
    assert invoice_total(inv) == Decimal("119.00")


def test_discount_whole_numbers():
    inv = build_invoice("A3", [("x", "100.00", 1, percent_off("TEN", "10"))])
    assert invoice_total(inv) == Decimal("90.00")


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "price,percent,line_amount,rate,total",
    [
        ("0.05", "10", "0.05", None, "0.10"),
        ("0.03", "20", "0.02", None, "0.04"),
        ("0.05", "10", "0.05", "0.10", "0.11"),
        ("0.03", "20", "0.02", "0.25", "0.05"),
    ],
)
def test_discount_total_uses_rounded_displayed_lines(price, percent, line_amount, rate, total):
    discount = percent_off("SALE", percent)
    tax_rule = TaxRule("TEST", Decimal(rate)) if rate is not None else None
    inv = build_invoice("A4", [("x", price, 1, discount), ("y", price, 1, discount)], tax_rule)

    assert line_totals(inv) == [Decimal(line_amount), Decimal(line_amount)]
    assert invoice_total(inv) == Decimal(total)
    displayed_amounts = [Decimal(row.split()[-1]) for row in render(inv).splitlines()]
    assert displayed_amounts == [Decimal(line_amount), Decimal(line_amount), Decimal(total)]
    if tax_rule is None:
        assert invoice_total(inv) == sum(line_totals(inv))

"""Totals. The PDF renderer shows line_totals(); the amount charged is invoice_total()."""
from decimal import Decimal

from .discounts import apply_discount
from .invoice import Invoice
from .money import round_money
from .tax import tax_for


def line_totals(inv: Invoice) -> list[Decimal]:
    """Per-line amounts as printed on the invoice, discount applied per line."""
    return [apply_discount(li.unit_price * li.qty, li.discount) for li in inv.lines]


def invoice_total(inv: Invoice) -> Decimal:
    """Amount charged: sum of lines after discount, plus tax on that sum."""
    net = sum(line_totals(inv), Decimal("0.00"))
    return round_money(net + tax_for(net, inv.tax_rule))

import re
import unicodedata

_WS = re.compile(r"\s+")


def email_key(email):
    return email.strip().lower()


def name_key(name):
    """Key for matching names: case-folded, single spaces, no accents."""
    s = unicodedata.normalize("NFD", name.casefold())
    s = "".join(c for c in s if not unicodedata.category(c).startswith("M"))
    return _WS.sub(" ", s.strip())


def dedupe(records):
    """records: list of dicts with 'name' and 'email'. Returns survivors in first-seen order."""
    seen_names, seen_emails = {}, {}
    parents, originals = [], []

    def root(i):
        while parents[i] != i:
            parents[i] = parents[parents[i]]
            i = parents[i]
        return i

    for r in records:
        i = len(parents)
        parents.append(i)
        originals.append(r)
        nk, ek = name_key(r["name"]), email_key(r["email"])
        for seen, key in ((seen_names, nk), (seen_emails, ek)):
            if key in seen:
                a, b = root(i), root(seen[key])
                parents[max(a, b)] = min(a, b)
            seen[key] = i
    return [r for i, r in enumerate(originals) if root(i) == i]

+import pytest
+
+from contacts import dedupe
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("variant", ["Jose Nunez", "Jose\u0301 Nu\u0301n\u0303ez", "  JOSÉ\t NÚÑEZ  "])
+def test_unicode_names(variant):
+    records = [{"name": "José Núñez", "email": "first@example.com"},
+               {"name": variant, "email": "second@example.com"}]
+    assert dedupe(records) == [records[0]]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("names", [("Straße", "STRASSE"), ("Łukáš", "Łukas"), ("François", "Francois")])
+def test_other_accents_and_casefold(names):
+    records = [{"name": name, "email": f"{i}@example.com"} for i, name in enumerate(names)]
+    assert dedupe(records) == [records[0]]
+
+
+def test_discarded_aliases_and_bridge_keep_first_survivor():
+    records = [{"name": "First", "email": "a@example.com"},
+               {"name": "Second", "email": "b@example.com"},
+               {"name": "FIRST", "email": " B@EXAMPLE.COM "},
+               {"name": "Third", "email": "b@example.com"},
+               {"name": "THIRD", "email": "c@example.com"},
+               {"name": "Independent", "email": "d@example.com"}]
+    result = dedupe(records)
+    assert result == [records[0], records[5]]
+    assert result[0] is records[0]

import pytest

from contacts import dedupe


@pytest.mark.parametrize("variant", ["Jose Nunez", "Jose\u0301 Nu\u0301n\u0303ez", "  JOSÉ\t NÚÑEZ  "])
def test_unicode_names(variant):
    records = [{"name": "José Núñez", "email": "first@example.com"},
               {"name": variant, "email": "second@example.com"}]
    assert dedupe(records) == [records[0]]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("names", [("Straße", "STRASSE"), ("Łukáš", "Łukas"), ("François", "Francois")])
def test_other_accents_and_casefold(names):
    records = [{"name": name, "email": f"{i}@example.com"} for i, name in enumerate(names)]
    assert dedupe(records) == [records[0]]


def test_discarded_aliases_and_bridge_keep_first_survivor():
    records = [{"name": "First", "email": "a@example.com"},
               {"name": "Second", "email": "b@example.com"},
               {"name": "FIRST", "email": " B@EXAMPLE.COM "},
               {"name": "Third", "email": "b@example.com"},
               {"name": "THIRD", "email": "c@example.com"},
               {"name": "Independent", "email": "d@example.com"}]
    result = dedupe(records)
    assert result == [records[0], records[5]]
    assert result[0] is records[0]

+import unittest
+
+from resolver import Constraint, ResolutionError, Version, resolve
+
+
+class ResolverTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_versions(self):
+        self.assertEqual(Version("1"), Version("1.0.0"))
+        self.assertEqual(hash(Version("1")), hash(Version("1.0")))
+        self.assertGreater(Version("1.10"), Version("1.9"))
+        self.assertGreater(Version("1.0.1"), Version("1"))
+        self.assertEqual(str(Version("01.0")), "01.0")
+
+    def test_constraints(self):
+        constraint = Constraint.parse("json>=2,<3,!=2.5")
+        self.assertEqual(constraint.name, "json")
+        for version, expected in [("1", False), ("2", True), ("2.5", False), ("3", False)]:
+            self.assertEqual(constraint.allows(Version(version)), expected)
+        for requirement, version, expected in [
+            ("a==1", "1.0", True), ("a<=1", "1.1", False),
+            ("a>1", "1.1", True), ("a", "999", True),
+        ]:
+            self.assertEqual(Constraint.parse(requirement).allows(Version(version)), expected)
+
+    def test_backtracking(self):
+        index = {
+            "app": {"1.0": ["web>=2", "db"]},
+            "web": {"1.0": [], "2.0": ["json<3"], "2.1": ["json>=3"]},
+            "json": {"2.0": [], "3.0": []},
+            "db": {"1.0": ["json<3"]},
+        }
+        self.assertEqual(resolve(["app"], index),
+                         {"app": "1.0", "db": "1.0", "json": "2.0", "web": "2.0"})
+
+    def test_global_preference(self):
+        index = {"z": {"2": ["a==1"], "1": ["a==2"]}, "a": {"1": [], "2": []}}
+        self.assertEqual(resolve(["z"], index), {"a": "2", "z": "1"})
+
+    def test_cycles_and_conflicting_cycles(self):
+        index = {"a": {"2": ["b"], "1": ["b"]}, "b": {"1": ["a<2"]}}
+        self.assertEqual(resolve(["a"], index), {"a": "1", "b": "1"})
+        self.assertEqual(resolve(["a"], {"a": {"1": ["a"]}}), {"a": "1"})
+
+    def test_dead_end_names_leaf(self):
+        for index in [{"a": {"1": ["b<1"]}, "b": {"1": [], "2": []}},
+                      {"a": {"1": ["b"]}}]:
+            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ResolutionError, "package b"):
+                resolve(["a"], index)
+
+    def test_roots_and_unreachable_packages(self):
+        index = {"a": {"1": [], "2": []}, "unused": {"9": []}}
+        self.assertEqual(resolve(["a>=1", "a<2"], index), {"a": "1"})
+        self.assertEqual(resolve([], index), {})
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ResolutionError, "a"):
+            resolve(["a>2"], index)
+

import re
from functools import total_ordering


class ResolutionError(Exception):
    pass


@total_ordering
class Version:
    def __init__(self, s):
        if not re.fullmatch(r"\d+(?:\.\d+)*", s):
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid version: {s!r}")
        self.original = s
        parts = tuple(int(part) for part in s.split("."))
        while len(parts) > 1 and parts[-1] == 0:
            parts = parts[:-1]
        self.parts = parts

    def __str__(self):
        return self.original

    def __eq__(self, other):
        if not isinstance(other, Version):
            return NotImplemented
        return self.parts == other.parts

    def __lt__(self, other):
        if not isinstance(other, Version):
            return NotImplemented
        return self.parts < other.parts

    def __hash__(self):
        return hash(self.parts)


class Constraint:
    @classmethod
    def parse(cls, requirement):
        match = re.fullmatch(r"\s*([^\s<>=!,]+)\s*(.*?)\s*", requirement)
        if not match:
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid requirement: {requirement!r}")
        result = cls()
        result.name = match[1]
        result.bounds = []
        if match[2]:
            for bound in match[2].split(","):
                parsed = re.fullmatch(r"\s*(==|!=|<=|>=|<|>)\s*(\d+(?:\.\d+)*)\s*", bound)
                if not parsed:
                    raise ValueError(f"Invalid requirement: {requirement!r}")
                result.bounds.append((parsed[1], Version(parsed[2])))
        return result

    def allows(self, version):
        for op, target in self.bounds:
            allowed = {
                "==": version == target,
                "!=": version != target,
                "<": version < target,
                "<=": version <= target,
                ">": version > target,
                ">=": version >= target,
            }[op]
            if not allowed:
                return False
        return True


def resolve(roots, index):
    versions = {
        name: sorted((Version(v) for v in releases), reverse=True)
        for name, releases in index.items()
    }
    dependencies = {
        (name, v): [Constraint.parse(r) for r in requirements]
        for name, releases in index.items()
        for v, requirements in releases.items()
    }
    constraints = {}
    for requirement in roots:
        constraint = Constraint.parse(requirement)
        constraints.setdefault(constraint.name, []).append(constraint)
    names = sorted(set(index) | set(constraints))
    best = None
    best_score = None
    dead_end = None

    def search(chosen, required):
        nonlocal best, best_score, dead_end
        candidates = {}
        for name, bounds in required.items():
            available = [chosen[name]] if name in chosen else versions.get(name, [])
            candidates[name] = [v for v in available if all(c.allows(v) for c in bounds)]
            if not candidates[name]:
                dead_end = name
                return

        # Bound the score using every package that could still become reachable.
        # Dependencies of unchosen releases are possibilities, not requirements.
        possible = dict(candidates)
        pending = list(possible)
        while pending:
            name = pending.pop()
            for version in possible[name]:
                for dependency in dependencies[(name, str(version))]:
                    if dependency.name not in possible:
                        possible[dependency.name] = versions.get(dependency.name, [])
                        pending.append(dependency.name)
        upper = tuple(max(possible[name]).parts if possible.get(name) else () for name in names)
        if best_score is not None and upper <= best_score:
            return

        remaining = sorted(set(required) - set(chosen))
        if not remaining:
            best = {name: str(version) for name, version in chosen.items()}
            best_score = tuple(chosen[name].parts if name in chosen else () for name in names)
            return
        name = remaining[0]
        for version in candidates[name]:
            next_chosen = dict(chosen, **{name: version})
            next_required = {package: list(bounds) for package, bounds in required.items()}
            for dependency in dependencies[(name, str(version))]:
                next_required.setdefault(dependency.name, []).append(dependency)
            search(next_chosen, next_required)

    search({}, constraints)
    if best is None:
        raise ResolutionError(f"Cannot satisfy constraints for package {dead_end}")
    return best

import unittest

from resolver import Constraint, ResolutionError, Version, resolve


class ResolverTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_versions(self):
        self.assertEqual(Version("1"), Version("1.0.0"))
        self.assertEqual(hash(Version("1")), hash(Version("1.0")))
        self.assertGreater(Version("1.10"), Version("1.9"))
        self.assertGreater(Version("1.0.1"), Version("1"))
        self.assertEqual(str(Version("01.0")), "01.0")

    def test_constraints(self):
        constraint = Constraint.parse("json>=2,<3,!=2.5")
        self.assertEqual(constraint.name, "json")
        for version, expected in [("1", False), ("2", True), ("2.5", False), ("3", False)]:
            self.assertEqual(constraint.allows(Version(version)), expected)
        for requirement, version, expected in [
            ("a==1", "1.0", True), ("a<=1", "1.1", False),
            ("a>1", "1.1", True), ("a", "999", True),
        ]:
            self.assertEqual(Constraint.parse(requirement).allows(Version(version)), expected)

    def test_backtracking(self):
        index = {
            "app": {"1.0": ["web>=2", "db"]},
            "web": {"1.0": [], "2.0": ["json<3"], "2.1": ["json>=3"]},
            "json": {"2.0": [], "3.0": []},
            "db": {"1.0": ["json<3"]},
        }
        self.assertEqual(resolve(["app"], index),
                         {"app": "1.0", "db": "1.0", "json": "2.0", "web": "2.0"})

    def test_global_preference(self):
        index = {"z": {"2": ["a==1"], "1": ["a==2"]}, "a": {"1": [], "2": []}}
        self.assertEqual(resolve(["z"], index), {"a": "2", "z": "1"})

    def test_cycles_and_conflicting_cycles(self):
        index = {"a": {"2": ["b"], "1": ["b"]}, "b": {"1": ["a<2"]}}
        self.assertEqual(resolve(["a"], index), {"a": "1", "b": "1"})
        self.assertEqual(resolve(["a"], {"a": {"1": ["a"]}}), {"a": "1"})

    def test_dead_end_names_leaf(self):
        for index in [{"a": {"1": ["b<1"]}, "b": {"1": [], "2": []}},
                      {"a": {"1": ["b"]}}]:
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ResolutionError, "package b"):
                resolve(["a"], index)

    def test_roots_and_unreachable_packages(self):
        index = {"a": {"1": [], "2": []}, "unused": {"9": []}}
        self.assertEqual(resolve(["a>=1", "a<2"], index), {"a": "1"})
        self.assertEqual(resolve([], index), {})
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ResolutionError, "a"):
            resolve(["a>2"], index)

    def test_discarded_dependencies(self):
        index = {"a": {"2": ["missing"], "1": ["b"]}, "b": {"1": []}}
        self.assertEqual(resolve(["a"], index), {"a": "1", "b": "1"})

    def test_many_versions(self):
        index = {name: {str(v): [] for v in range(100)} for name in ["a", "b", "c", "d"]}
        self.assertEqual(resolve(list(index), index), {name: "99" for name in index})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Drop duplicate events (the collector retries, so the same event_id can appear several times).

Refactored to keep insertion order of first occurrence, which the old set-based version did not guarantee.
"""


def dedupe_rows(rows):
    seen_ids = set()
    out = []
    for r in rows:
        if r.event_id in seen_ids:
            continue
        seen_ids.add(r.event_id)
        out.append(r)
    return out

+from reporting.dedupe import dedupe_rows
+from reporting.model import UsageRow
+
+
+class CountingEventId(str):
+    comparisons = 0
+    __hash__ = str.__hash__
+
+    def __eq__(self, other):
+        type(self).comparisons += 1
+        return super().__eq__(other)
+
+
+def test_dedupe_preserves_first_occurrence_with_linear_membership_work():
+    count = 1000
+    rows = [
+        UsageRow(CountingEventId(str(i)), "tenant", "service", float(i), i)
+        for i in range(count)
+    ]
+    duplicates = [
+        UsageRow(CountingEventId(str(i)), "other", "other", 0.0, 0)
+        for i in reversed(range(count))
+    ]
+    CountingEventId.comparisons = 0
+
+    result = dedupe_rows(iter(rows + duplicates))
+    comparisons = CountingEventId.comparisons
+
+    assert len(result) == count
+    assert all(actual is expected for actual, expected in zip(result, rows))
+    # Count work instead of elapsed time so slow CI machines do not cause failures.
+    assert comparisons < count * 4

Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEvery response, whole session, until user says \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present. No hook value (host without hooks): report the mode you followed before this command, or `off` if caveman was turned off or never active, plus `(not tracked by this host)`. Example: `Caveman mode: caveman (not tracked by this host)`. Loading this skill to answer status is not activation. Never infer a mode from the configured default.\n\n## Why\n\n1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.\n2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.\n3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.\n\nBad: \"Migration drop column backup first.\"\nGood: \"Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column.\"\n\n### 5. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. Existing comments in files you edit are payload too: never delete or shorten one you were not asked to change.\n\n### 7. Tool runs: bounded status\n\nNo text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.\n\n### 8. User's language\n\nCompress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.\n\n### 9. Never perform caveman\n\nNo \"caveman mode on\", no \"me think\", no \"Caveman:\" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.\n\n## When to break the rules\n\nPlain prose, then resume:\n\n1. Security warning.\n2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.\n3. Step order a fragment could scramble.\n4. User confused or repeats the question.\n5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.\n6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.\n7. You ask the user a question or offer options. Full sentences, so the answer comes back right first time.\n\n## Pre-send check\n\n1. First sentence announces what you will do? Delete.\n2. Last sentence recaps or offers help? Delete.\n3. from reporting.dedupe import dedupe_rows
from reporting.model import UsageRow


class CountingEventId(str):
    comparisons = 0
    __hash__ = str.__hash__

    def __eq__(self, other):
        type(self).comparisons += 1
        return super().__eq__(other)


def test_dedupe_preserves_first_occurrence_with_linear_membership_work():
    count = 1000
    rows = [
        UsageRow(CountingEventId(str(i)), "tenant", "service", float(i), i)
        for i in range(count)
    ]
    duplicates = [
        UsageRow(CountingEventId(str(i)), "other", "other", 0.0, 0)
        for i in reversed(range(count))
    ]
    CountingEventId.comparisons = 0

    result = dedupe_rows(iter(rows + duplicates))
    comparisons = CountingEventId.comparisons

    assert len(result) == count
    assert all(actual is expected for actual, expected in zip(result, rows))
    # Count work instead of elapsed time so slow CI machines do not cause failures.
    assert comparisons < count * 4

from copy import deepcopy
import re


class PatchError(Exception):
    pass


class PointerError(PatchError):
    pass


def _tokens(pointer):
    if not isinstance(pointer, str):
        raise PointerError('Pointer must be a string')
    if pointer == '':
        return []
    if not pointer.startswith('/'):
        raise PointerError('Pointer must start with /')
    tokens = pointer[1:].split('/')
    for token in tokens:
        if re.search(r'~(?:[^01]|$)', token):
            raise PointerError('Invalid pointer escape')
    return [token.replace('~1', '/').replace('~0', '~') for token in tokens]


def _index(token, length, adding=False):
    if adding and token == '-':
        return length
    if re.fullmatch(r'0|[1-9][0-9]*', token) is None:
        raise PointerError('Invalid array index')
    # Compare strings first to avoid Python's limit on integer conversion.
    limit = str(length if adding else length - 1)
    if length == 0 and not adding or len(token) > len(limit) or (len(token) == len(limit) and token > limit):
        raise PointerError('Array index out of bounds')
    return int(token)


def _resolve(doc, tokens):
    for token in tokens:
        if isinstance(doc, dict):
            if token not in doc:
                raise PointerError('Object key does not exist')
            doc = doc[token]
        elif isinstance(doc, list):
            doc = doc[_index(token, len(doc))]
        else:
            raise PointerError('Cannot traverse a scalar')
    return doc


def resolve_pointer(doc, pointer):
    return _resolve(doc, _tokens(pointer))


def _edit(doc, tokens, op, value=None):
    if not tokens:
        return None if op == 'remove' else value
    parent = _resolve(doc, tokens[:-1])
    token = tokens[-1]
    if isinstance(parent, dict):
        if op != 'add' and token not in parent:
            raise PointerError('Object key does not exist')
        if op == 'remove':
            del parent[token]
        else:
            parent[token] = value
    elif isinstance(parent, list):
        index = _index(token, len(parent), adding=op == 'add')
        if op == 'add':
            parent.insert(index, value)
        elif op == 'remove':
            parent.pop(index)
        else:
            parent[index] = value
    else:
        raise PointerError('Target parent is a scalar')
    return doc


def _equal(left, right):
    if isinstance(left, bool) or isinstance(right, bool):
        return type(left) is type(right) and left == right
    if isinstance(left, (int, float)) and isinstance(right, (int, float)):
        return left == right
    if type(left) is not type(right):
        return False
    if isinstance(left, list):
        return len(left) == len(right) and all(_equal(a, b) for a, b in zip(left, right))
    if isinstance(left, dict):
        return left.keys() == right.keys() and all(_equal(left[key], right[key]) for key in left)
    return left == right


def apply_patch(doc, patch, in_place=False):
    if not isinstance(patch, list):
        raise PatchError('Patch must be a list')
    result = deepcopy(doc)
    for operation in patch:
        if not isinstance(operation, dict):
            raise PatchError('Operation must be an object')
        op = operation.get('op')
        if not isinstance(op, str) or op not in ('add', 'remove', 'replace', 'move', 'copy', 'test'):
            raise PatchError('Unknown operation')
        if 'path' not in operation:
            raise PatchError('Missing path')
        path = _tokens(operation['path'])
        if op in ('add', 'replace', 'test'):
            if 'value' not in operation:
                raise PatchError('Missing value')
            value = deepcopy(operation['value'])
        if op in ('move', 'copy'):
            if 'from' not in operation:
                raise PatchError('Missing from')
            source = _tokens(operation['from'])
            value = _resolve(result, source)
            if op == 'move':
                if len(source) < len(path) and path[:len(source)] == source:
                    raise PatchError('Cannot move a value into its child')
                result = _edit(result, source, 'remove')
            else:
                value = deepcopy(value)
            result = _edit(result, path, 'add', value)
        elif op == 'test':
            if not _equal(_resolve(result, path), value):
                raise PatchError('Test failed')
        elif op == 'remove':
            result = _edit(result, path, op)
        else:
            result = _edit(result, path, op, value)
    if in_place:
        if isinstance(doc, dict) and isinstance(result, dict):
            doc.clear()
            doc.update(result)
            return doc
        if isinstance(doc, list) and isinstance(result, list):
            doc[:] = result
            return doc
    return result

@@ -0,0 +1,81 @@
+import unittest
+from copy import deepcopy
+
+from jsonpatch.core import PatchError, PointerError, apply_patch, resolve_pointer
+
+
+class PointerTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_resolution(self):
+        doc = {'a/b': {'~key': [3]}, '': 4, '~1': 5}
+        self.assertIs(resolve_pointer(doc, ''), doc)
+        self.assertEqual(resolve_pointer(doc, '/a~1b/~0key/0'), 3)
+        self.assertEqual(resolve_pointer(doc, '/'), 4)
+        self.assertEqual(resolve_pointer(doc, '/~01'), 5)
+
+    def test_invalid(self):
+        for pointer in (None, 'x', '/~', '/~2', '/missing', '/a/-', '/a/01', '/a/-1', '/a/1', '/a/٠', '/a/0/x'):
+            with self.subTest(pointer=pointer), self.assertRaises(PointerError):
+                resolve_pointer({'a': [1]}, pointer)
+
+
+class PatchTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_all_operations(self):
+        doc = {'a': [1, 2], 'b': {'x': 3}}
+        patch = [
+            {'op': 'add', 'path': '/a/-', 'value': 4},
+            {'op': 'add', 'path': '/a/1', 'value': 9},
+            {'op': 'remove', 'path': '/a/0'},
+            {'op': 'replace', 'path': '/b/x', 'value': 5},
+            {'op': 'copy', 'from': '/b', 'path': '/c'},
+            {'op': 'move', 'from': '/a/0', 'path': '/a/2'},
+            {'op': 'test', 'path': '/a', 'value': [2, 4, 9]},
+        ]
+        result = apply_patch(doc, patch)
+        self.assertEqual(result, {'a': [2, 4, 9], 'b': {'x': 5}, 'c': {'x': 5}})
+        result['c']['x'] = 8
+        self.assertEqual(result['b']['x'], 5)
+        self.assertEqual(doc, {'a': [1, 2], 'b': {'x': 3}})
+
+    def test_atomic_failure(self):
+        for in_place in (False, True):
+            doc = {'a': [1]}
+            original = deepcopy(doc)
+            with self.assertRaises(PatchError):
+                apply_patch(doc, [{'op': 'add', 'path': '/a/-', 'value': 2}, {'op': 'remove', 'path': '/missing'}], in_place)
+            self.assertEqual(doc, original)
+
+    def test_in_place(self):
+        for doc, path in (({}, '/a'), ([], '/-')):
+            result = apply_patch(doc, [{'op': 'add', 'path': path, 'value': 1}], True)

Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEvery response, whole session, until user says \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present. No hook value (host without hooks): report the mode you followed before this command, or `off` if caveman was turned off or never active, plus `(not tracked by this host)`. Example: `Caveman mode: caveman (not tracked by this host)`. Loading this skill to answer status is not activation. Never infer a mode from the configured default.\n\n## Why\n\n1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.\n2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.\n3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. Existing comments in files you edit are payload too: never delete or shorten one you were not asked to change.\n\n### 7. Tool runs: bounded status\n\nNo text between routine calls. User's language\n\nCompress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.\n\n## When to break the rules\n\nPlain prose, then resume:\n\n1. Security warning.\n2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.\n3. Step order a fragment could scramble.\n4. User confused or repeats the question.\n5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.\n6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.\n7. You ask the user a question or offer options. Full sentences, so the answer comes back right first time.\n\n## Pre-send check\n\n1. First sentence announces what you will do? Delete.\n2. Last sentence recaps or offers help? Delete.\n3. self.assertTrue(doc)\n\n    def test_roots(self):\n        self.assertEqual(apply_patch({}, [{'op': 'add', 'path': '', 'value': [1]}]), [1])\n        self.assertEqual(apply_patch(1, [{'op': 'replace', apply_patch(actual, [{'op': 'test', 'path': '', 'value': expected}])\n\n    def test_invalid_operations(self):\n        cases = (None, {}, [None], [{}], [{'op': []}], [{'op': 'unknown', 'path': import unittest
from copy import deepcopy

from jsonpatch.core import PatchError, PointerError, apply_patch, resolve_pointer


class PointerTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_resolution(self):
        doc = {'a/b': {'~key': [3]}, '': 4, '~1': 5}
        self.assertIs(resolve_pointer(doc, ''), doc)
        self.assertEqual(resolve_pointer(doc, '/a~1b/~0key/0'), 3)
        self.assertEqual(resolve_pointer(doc, '/'), 4)
        self.assertEqual(resolve_pointer(doc, '/~01'), 5)

    def test_invalid(self):
        for pointer in (None, 'x', '/~', '/~2', '/missing', '/a/-', '/a/01', '/a/-1', '/a/1', '/a/٠', '/a/0/x'):
            with self.subTest(pointer=pointer), self.assertRaises(PointerError):
                resolve_pointer({'a': [1]}, pointer)


class PatchTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_all_operations(self):
        doc = {'a': [1, 2], 'b': {'x': 3}}
        patch = [
            {'op': 'add', 'path': '/a/-', 'value': 4},
            {'op': 'add', 'path': '/a/1', 'value': 9},
            {'op': 'remove', 'path': '/a/0'},
            {'op': 'replace', 'path': '/b/x', 'value': 5},
            {'op': 'copy', 'from': '/b', 'path': '/c'},
            {'op': 'move', 'from': '/a/0', 'path': '/a/2'},
            {'op': 'test', 'path': '/a', 'value': [2, 4, 9]},
        ]
        result = apply_patch(doc, patch)
        self.assertEqual(result, {'a': [2, 4, 9], 'b': {'x': 5}, 'c': {'x': 5}})
        result['c']['x'] = 8
        self.assertEqual(result['b']['x'], 5)
        self.assertEqual(doc, {'a': [1, 2], 'b': {'x': 3}})

    def test_atomic_failure(self):
        for in_place in (False, True):
            doc = {'a': [1]}
            original = deepcopy(doc)
            with self.assertRaises(PatchError):
                apply_patch(doc, [{'op': 'add', 'path': '/a/-', 'value': 2}, {'op': 'remove', 'path': '/missing'}], in_place)
            self.assertEqual(doc, original)

    def test_in_place(self):
        for doc, path in (({}, '/a'), ([], '/-')):
            result = apply_patch(doc, [{'op': 'add', 'path': path, 'value': 1}], True)
            self.assertIs(result, doc)
            self.assertTrue(doc)

    def test_roots(self):
        self.assertEqual(apply_patch({}, [{'op': 'add', 'path': '', 'value': [1]}]), [1])
        self.assertEqual(apply_patch(1, [{'op': 'replace', 'path': '', 'value': 2}]), 2)
        self.assertIsNone(apply_patch({}, [{'op': 'remove', 'path': ''}]))
        self.assertEqual(apply_patch({'a': 1}, [{'op': 'move', 'from': '/a', 'path': ''}]), 1)

    def test_move_validation(self):
        with self.assertRaises(PatchError):
            apply_patch({'a': {}}, [{'op': 'move', 'from': '/a', 'path': '/a/b'}])
        self.assertEqual(apply_patch({'a': 1}, [{'op': 'move', 'from': '/a', 'path': '/a'}]), {'a': 1})

    def test_equality(self):
        apply_patch({'a': [1, {'b': 2}]}, [{'op': 'test', 'path': '', 'value': {'a': [1.0, {'b': 2.0}]}}])
        for actual, expected in ((True, 1), ([True], [1]), ({'a': False}, {'a': 0}), (None, 0)):
            with self.assertRaises(PatchError):
                apply_patch(actual, [{'op': 'test', 'path': '', 'value': expected}])

    def test_invalid_operations(self):
        cases = (None, {}, [None], [{}], [{'op': []}], [{'op': 'unknown', 'path': ''}],
                 [{'op': 'add', 'path': ''}], [{'op': 'copy', 'path': ''}],
                 [{'op': 'remove', 'path': 1}], [{'op': 'replace', 'path': '/missing', 'value': 1}],
                 [{'op': 'add', 'path': '/2', 'value': 1}])
        for patch in cases:
            with self.subTest(patch=patch), self.assertRaises(PatchError):
                apply_patch([], patch)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()
